instruction.text: Read the text and answer the questions.

atoms.text: If you check the unconscious person’s breathing and find that they are not breathing, you should begin chest compressions.
To carry out chest compressions, place one hand on top of the other and interlock your fingers. Then, place the heel of your hand on the centre of the unconscious person’s chest.

Using straightened arms and your whole body weight, you should then press down on their chest by about 5cm. You should repeat compressions 30 times, with an even rhythm of around one compression per second.

atoms.a: How should the chest be pressed during compressions? Choose the three correct answers.
How should your hands be positioned for chest compressions?

instruction.text: Read the text and answer the question.

atoms.text: After 30 chest compressions, we begin rescue breaths or mouth-to-mouth. To do this, first tilt the person’s head back and clear their airway.
Next, pinch the person’s nostrils shut and take a deep breath in.
Then, blow into their mouth steadily and firmly for one second so that their chest rises.

You should give two rescue breaths. Then, you should resume chest compressions. These two actions together are called CPR. CPR should be carried out until the person resumes breathing or the emergency services take over.

instruction.text: Put the steps of giving a rescue breath in order.

atoms.b: First, tilt back the unconscious person’s head and open their mouth.
Then, pinch their nose shut and take a deep breath in.
Blow air into their mouth steadily and firmly for one second so their chest rises.
